biography.plain_text: Alberto Ravano was an Italian shipowner who established four shipping companies in Genoa during the 1920s and rebuilt his fleet after the Second World War. His business expanded internationally through the American company Tidewater Commercial. He also owned Sampdoria, serving as president from 1953 to 1961 and strengthening its place in Italian football.

long_biography.plain_text:
For shipowner Alberto Ravano, rebuilding meant committing money to new vessels as well as buying existing ships. He commissioned the tanker Clyde Water for £900,000, a substantial risk when it was launched in 1951. Its charter earnings covered that cost within two years. He also led the Italian delegation negotiating purchases of American Liberty ships after the war.

At Sampdoria, Ravano favoured attacking football and recruited players to match that ambition, including Austria's Ernst Ocwirk and Sweden's Lennart Skoglund. The team finished fourth in Serie A in 1960–61. Years later, fellow club president Paolo Mantovani named a children's football tournament in his memory.

Shipping origin is directly supported by personal company formation, fleet ownership and profitable charter operations. Terminal businesses span shipping, property, finance and agriculture, but their individual materiality and relative weight are not established. Primary industry is expressly the required origin-sector fallback, not a claim that terminal shipping dominance was proved.

Founder is a medium-confidence inference from personally created substantial core, continued fleet investment immediately before death and explicit retained shipping enterprises in his estate. It does not assert daily management at death. Investor and Passive asset owner lack evidence of a principal changed allocation mandate or affirmative retirement/delegation; no exact balance sheet is required.

Broad Self-made rests on demonstrable personal formation and profitable expansion, not the absence of inheritance reporting. The Ravano family's pre-WWI ships and wife Luisa Accame's shipping lineage are real caveats. A materially transferred principal core or relevant substantial launch advantage is not established sufficiently to choose family transfer, Mixed or either self-made subtype.

Birth date and birthplace beyond the immutable Italy baseline remain unverified. Death year 1970 is supported by contemporary reporting and secondary corroboration, but exact day and month remain blank. The informal nickname Comandante is not proposed as a formal title.

Historical Monaco residence is reported explicitly in the 1976 article, but no robust independent address or residence document was found. Italy baseline is preserved rather than silently overwritten; this does not deny the reported move.

Forbes was searched first; no exact profile verified. All supported person-relevant link types were checked: LinkedIn, Instagram, Personal Website, Facebook, Twitter, Youtube, TikTok, Vimeo, Flickr, Wikipedia, Forbes and relevant Company Website. Results concern living HSBC or commodity-business namesakes, third-party football histories, memorial tournament accounts and unrelated individuals. No deceased-owner personal account or dedicated authoritative personal Wikipedia page was verified. Trip Advisor and Zillow have no relevant fit.

The existing football club's website supports historical research, but he neither currently owns nor leads it, so no present Company Website link is proposed. The memorial tournament is a distinct later organisation.

Primary museum and specialist fleet history differ on a Seafox construction date, and the museum's rendering of the Saglietto representative's forename differs. Neither disputed detail is used. The specialist's post-1970 use of Alberto's name denotes continuing family companies, not his own posthumous activity.

Three active tags meet literal contracts: substantial controlled dry-cargo and tanker operations, and sustained eight-year football ownership/governance. Broader maritime, incidental property or finance interests and sailing recreation add insufficient distinct supported cohort value.

Biographies use only directly supported business and sporting facts. They omit inheritance claims, terminal asset rankings, family criminal allegations, yacht relationships and descendants' activities. Long-only mechanisms and the memorial's named founder prevent a repeated institutional chronology.
